newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Race against time to build Hong Kong handover venue.
newsitem.headline: Race against time to build Hong Kong handover venue.

text.p: Hong Kong is racing against the clock to meet a deadline it cannot afford to miss -- the completion of an ambitious structure where ceremonies marking the handover to China will take place in just 69 days.
Against a backdrop of towering bamboo scaffolding and workers pouring cement, Hong Kong Convention Centre chief executive Niels Kraunsoe said he was confident the doors would open on time.

"We're six weeks away from completion," he told reporters on Wednesday as they picked their way through the clutter of construction at the HK$4.8 billion (US$620 million) extension to the existing Convention Centre.
"Every construction project I've worked on in 27 years has been a rush."

At five storeys, the extension is a squat anomaly alongside the towers of Hong Kong. But handover ceremony guests and future convention-goers will get a panoramic view of one of the world's busiest harbours and most spectacular skylines.
"We have a wonderful location so we have to have a building that's worthy of that location," Kraunsoe said.
The extension, built on reclaimed land, is surrounded on three sides by the harbour and sits in front of the existing convention centre. A bridge connects the two buildings.

The rounded outer shell of the extension is almost complete. The inner floors, walls, windows and escalators are in place. Marble and carpet has been laid in some places but stacks of plasterboard, bales of insulation and crates of Italian stone cover others.

The multi-layered curved roof -- inspired by a bird soaring into flight -- should be finished in mid-May when the last of its aluminium cladding is attached, deputy project director Patrick Kwan told Reuters.

On the evening of June 30, more than 4,000 VIPs from around the world will fill the Grand Hall for a gala banquet before they witness Prince Charles handing over Britain's last major colony to China in a midnight ceremony.
The Grand Hall now resembles a hangar at the territory's Kai Tak airport rather than the venue for the solemn and historical transfer of sovereignty.
"There's a lot of work to be done in this room," Kraunsoe said. The handover ceremony will be staged in the adjoining glassed-in Grand Foyer which juts out into Victoria Harbour.
The 3,000 workers from a dozen trades have been working "quite a lot" of overtime to get meet the deadline, Kwan said.
"The building is so big. The time for construction is so little. That makes everything so tough," he said.

The building is being developed by the territory's quasi-governmental Trade Development Council (TDC) and funded by the taxpayer. The work is being done by local construction company Hip Hing Construction Co Ltd and Dragages et Travaux Publics of France.
